text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Parliament ready to impose 1,000 markka ceiling on monthly child daycare charges.
- Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari, on trip to India, said Finland disappointed India did not join nuclear test ban.
- Finnish income differences have held stable for the past ten years and did not widen even during the recession of the 1990s, statistics show. @
- Transport workers union's boycott of Russian cargo came to a head yesterday as Russian transport minister threatened to cancel a visit to Finland next week if the boycott continued.
- Last year Finland paid almost one billion markka more to the European Union than it received, according to EU auditors.
- Drunks' slurred speach is due to the way the 'S' sound invades other sounds, says linguist in new dissertation.
- Over 4,000 small service-sector firms were established last year in Finland last year, official statistics show, and new firms are still being created at a steady pace. @

- Government takes a time-out in preparations for new legislation on the Bank of Finland. The new law is expected to change the role of the parliamentary bank supervisors and concentrate power over monetary policy in the bank's board.
- Salomon Brother analysts see little upside left in Nordic banking shares.
- Production chief of Russian car maker Avtovaz says company's cooperation agreement with Finnish Valmet is technically sound, but too expensive. @
- Butchers say Christmas ham to be more expensive than last year. Cheaper imported Danish pork one alternative.
- Sale of Finnish armoured personnel carriers to Indonesia stalled due to a competitive offer from British company.
- Central Union of Agricultural Producers MTK chairman Esa Harmala says farm sector should draw up a cost control programme to prepare for EMU.
